1.title: Paul and Timothy to Colossae
1.context: Paul writes with Timothy to a church in Colossae, a city in the Lycus valley of Asia Minor. Paul had never visited it; the letter itself says he struggled for people who had not met him face to face.
1.question: What does it mean to you that a letter this warm was written to people the writer had never met?

1.title: Thanks for Faith and Love Heard About
1.context: Paul's thanksgiving rests on a report. News of the Colossians' faith and love traveled to the imprisoned apostle, and his first response was prayer and thanks.
1.question: Whose faith have you only heard about, and how could you thank God for them this week?

1.title: The Hope Stored Up in Heaven
1.context: Paul traces faith and love back to hope: a hope already stored up in heaven, first heard in the gospel message. In his letters, what God has prepared ahead shapes how believers live now.
1.question: How does a hope stored up for you change the way you face an ordinary day?

1.title: Bearing Fruit All Over the World
1.context: Paul pictures the gospel as a living, growing thing, bearing fruit across the world just as it had in Colossae since the day the Colossians first heard it and understood God's grace.
1.question: Where have you seen the gospel quietly bearing fruit over time?

1.title: Epaphras, Who Taught and Reported
1.context: Epaphras was a Colossian who carried the gospel home to his own people and later reported their love back to Paul. He is a different man from Epaphroditus, the messenger in Philippians.
1.question: Who has carried good news to you, and who might need you to carry their story to someone else?

2.title: Praying Without Stopping
2.context: Since the day the report arrived, Paul says, the praying has not stopped. The ask is specific: to be filled with the knowledge of God's will, with spiritual wisdom and understanding.
2.question: What would it look like to pray for one person this steadily?

2.title: A Walk Worthy of the Lord
2.context: Walk is Paul's picture for the whole of a life. The prayer's goal is a walk that pleases the Lord, bearing fruit in good works and growing in the knowledge of God.
2.question: What is one step of your walk that you want to be worthy of the Lord?

2.title: Strengthened to Endure, Joyfully
2.context: The strength Paul prays for is aimed at endurance and patience, and it ends in thanksgiving to the Father, who has qualified his people to share in the inheritance of the saints in the light.
2.question: Where do you need endurance more than escape right now?

2.title: Rescued from Darkness
2.context: Paul describes salvation as a transfer between kingdoms: rescued from the dominion of darkness and brought into the kingdom of God's beloved Son.
2.question: What has God already rescued you from, that you can thank him for today?

2.title: Redemption, the Forgiveness of Sins
2.context: Redemption was the price paid to free someone enslaved. Paul defines it directly as the forgiveness of sins, located in the Son.
2.question: Is there a sin you still carry as if it had not been forgiven?

3.title: The Image of the Invisible God
3.context: This passage is often called the Christ hymn. It begins with the Son as the image of the invisible God and firstborn over all creation, language of rank and honor.
3.question: What does it change for you that God has made himself visible in his Son?

3.title: All Things Created Through Him and for Him
3.context: The hymn sweeps up everything, heaven and earth, visible and invisible, every throne and authority, as created in, through, and for Christ, who is before all things and holds all things together.
3.question: How does Christ holding all things together speak to what feels scattered in your life?

3.title: Head of the Body, Firstborn from the Dead
3.context: The hymn turns to the church: Christ is its head, the beginning and firstborn from among the dead, so that in everything he has the preeminence, with all God's fullness dwelling in him.
3.question: What would it mean for Christ to have first place in one crowded corner of your life?

3.title: Peace Through the Blood of His Cross
3.context: Reconciliation reaches as wide as creation: all things, on earth and in heaven, reconciled to God, with peace made through the blood of Christ's cross.
3.question: Where do you most need the peace this verse describes?

3.title: Once Alienated, Now Reconciled
3.context: Paul applies the hymn to his readers: once alienated and hostile in mind, now reconciled through Christ's death, called to continue established and firm in the faith they heard.
3.question: What helps you stay established and firm when your faith feels moved?

4.title: Rejoicing in Sufferings for the Church
4.context: Paul speaks of his sufferings as service to Christ's body, the church, and says he rejoices in them. He does not explain the mystery of that further; he states it and moves on.
4.question: How do you respond to the idea that suffering for others can hold joy?

4.title: The Mystery Hidden for Ages
4.context: Paul's commission was to proclaim God's word fully, including the mystery hidden for ages and generations but now revealed to God's saints.
4.question: What truth about God has only become clear to you with time?

4.title: Christ in You, the Hope of Glory
4.context: The revealed mystery is Christ in you, the hope of glory, made known among the Gentiles. Paul's labor aims at presenting everyone perfect in Christ, striving with Christ's own energy.
4.question: What does Christ in you, the hope of glory, stir in you today?

4.title: Struggling for People Never Met
4.context: Paul struggles for the Colossians, the Laodiceans, and all who have not met him, that their hearts may be encouraged, knit together in love, and know Christ, in whom all wisdom's treasures are hidden.
4.question: Who could you struggle for in prayer even though you may never meet them?

4.title: No One Deceive You by Smooth Rhetoric
4.context: The encouragement turns to warning: fine sounding arguments were in the air. Absent in body, Paul says he is present in spirit, delighting in their orderly condition and firm faith.
4.question: How do you tell the difference between smooth rhetoric and the truth you already know?

5.title: Continue to Walk in Him
5.context: Received is the starting point: just as they received Christ Jesus as Lord, they are to keep walking in him, rooted like a tree and built up like a building, overflowing with thankfulness.
5.question: What would continuing in Christ, rather than starting over, look like for you this week?

5.title: See to It That No One Takes You Captive
5.context: Paul warns against being carried off captive by philosophy and empty deception based on human tradition and the spiritual forces of the world rather than on Christ. He never names the teaching or its teachers.
5.question: What ideas compete to define your life apart from Christ?

5.title: Made Complete in Christ
5.context: All the fullness of the Deity dwells in Christ in bodily form, and believers have been made complete in him, the head over every ruler and authority. Completeness answers the suggestion that something is missing.
5.question: Where are you most tempted to believe you are incomplete without something more?

5.title: Buried with Him, Raised with Him
5.context: Paul ties their story to Christ's: a circumcision performed by Christ and not by human hands, burial with him in baptism, raised with him through faith in God's power, made alive and forgiven.
5.question: Which past tense truth about you do you most need to remember today?

5.title: The Debt Nailed to the Cross
5.context: The record of debt that stood against them was canceled and nailed to the cross, and the powers and authorities were disarmed and made a public spectacle, triumphed over by the cross.
5.question: What record against you do you need to leave nailed where God put it?

6.title: A Shadow, and the Body That Casts It
6.context: Food, drink, festivals, New Moons, and Sabbaths are called a shadow of things to come; the body that casts the shadow belongs to Christ. Shadows in Scripture point beyond themselves.
6.question: Are there religious rules you treat as the substance instead of Christ himself?

6.title: Holding Fast to the Head
6.context: False humility, the worship of angels, and speculation about visions can disqualify, Paul says, when they disconnect a person from the head, Christ, from whom the whole body grows as God makes it grow.
6.question: What helps you stay connected to Christ rather than impressed by spiritual display?

6.title: Why Submit to Its Regulations?
6.context: Having died with Christ to the spiritual forces of the world, the Colossians are asked why they live as if they still belonged to it, submitting to its regulations.
6.question: What old rule do you still obey as if your life depended on it?

6.title: Do Not Handle, Do Not Taste, Do Not Touch
6.context: The quoted regulations are all prohibitions about things that perish with use, resting on human commands and teachings rather than on God.
6.question: Have you ever confused avoiding things with growing in holiness? What came of it?

6.title: An Appearance of Wisdom
6.context: Paul concedes the restrictions look wise, with self prescribed worship, false humility, and harsh treatment of the body, but finds them of no value against the indulgence of the flesh.
6.question: Where might something in your life have the appearance of wisdom without its power?

7.title: Your Life Is Hidden with Christ
7.context: Raised with Christ, believers are told to strive for the things above, where Christ sits at God's right hand. Their life is hidden with Christ in God, and when Christ appears, they will appear with him in glory.
7.question: How does a life hidden with Christ change what you strive for?

7.title: Put to Death What Is Earthly
7.context: The earthly nature's components are listed plainly, from sexual immorality to greed, which Paul calls idolatry. God's wrath comes because of these, and the Colossians once walked in them too.
7.question: Which item on Paul's list do you find easiest to excuse in yourself?

7.title: Taken Off the Old Self
7.context: Anger, rage, malice, slander, and filthy language are to be put aside, and lying with them, because the old self with its practices has been taken off like a garment.
7.question: What piece of the old self do you most need to leave off today?

7.title: Put On the New Self
7.context: The new self is being renewed in knowledge in the image of its Creator. Renewal is present tense: a person remade after the pattern of the image of God.
7.question: In what way is your new self being renewed right now?

7.title: Christ Is All and Is in All
7.context: In the new humanity the old divisions, Greek and Jew, circumcised and uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave and free, give way to one fact: Christ is all and is in all.
7.question: Which human category do you lean on most for your sense of worth?

8.title: Over All These, Put On Love
8.context: As God's elect, holy and beloved, the Colossians are to clothe themselves with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience, forgiving as the Lord forgave them, and over all, love, the bond of perfect unity.
8.question: Which of these garments is hardest for you to put on, and toward whom?

8.title: The Word of Christ Richly Dwelling
8.context: The peace of Christ is to rule in their hearts, and the word of Christ to dwell richly among them, coming out in teaching, admonishing, and singing, with everything done in the name of the Lord Jesus.
8.question: How could the word of Christ dwell more richly in your home this week?

8.title: The Household, Addressed Pair by Pair
8.context: Wives and husbands, children and fathers are each addressed directly, in both directions, each answerable to the Lord. The stronger party in each pair is the one told to hold back.
8.question: Which of these household words is spoken most directly to you?

8.title: As for the Lord and Not for Men
8.context: Slaves are told to work with sincerity of heart, as for the Lord rather than men, knowing the inheritance comes from him. The words have since encouraged workers of every kind; wrongdoing is repaid without favoritism.
8.question: How does working as for the Lord change a task you find thankless?

8.title: You Also Have a Master in Heaven
8.context: The household teaching ends with masters: supply what is right and fair, knowing they too have a Master in heaven. Authority is answered for, upward.
8.question: If you hold authority over anyone, what would right and fair look like from their side?

9.title: A Door for the Word
9.context: Devotion to prayer, watchful and thankful, comes first. Paul asks prayer not for release but for an open door for the word and clarity in proclaiming the mystery of Christ, for which he is in chains.
9.question: What open door could you pray for, for yourself or for someone else?

9.title: Tychicus and Onesimus Carry the News
9.context: Tychicus, beloved brother and faithful minister, carries this letter as he carried Ephesians. With him travels Onesimus, called faithful and beloved, one of the Colossians' own; his fuller story is told in Philemon.
9.question: Who carries news and encouragement between you and people you love?

9.title: Fellow Workers and a Comfort
9.context: Aristarchus the fellow prisoner, Mark the cousin of Barnabas, and Jesus called Justus send greetings. Paul calls these Jewish fellow workers a comfort to him, and Mark is to be welcomed if he comes.
9.question: Who has been a comfort to you in hard work, and have you told them?

9.title: Epaphras Wrestling in Prayer
9.context: Epaphras greets his own people and wrestles in prayer for their maturity. The letter is then to travel: read in Laodicea, whose letter the Colossians are to read in turn, and Archippus is charged to complete his ministry.
9.question: What ministry have you received that you want to complete well?

9.title: In My Own Hand: Remember My Chains
9.context: Paul takes the pen for the greeting himself, as he often did to sign his letters, and asks to be remembered in his chains. Grace is his last word to them.
9.question: Who in chains, literal or otherwise, could you remember this week?
